content.title: Reporting a Lost Bag
content.context_description: You will hear a woman phoning the lost property office of a city train service to report a bag she left on a train.

speakers.name: Claire
speakers.role: Train passenger reporting a lost bag

script.speaker: S1
script.text: Good afternoon, lost property office, Darren speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Oh, hello. Um, I left a bag on one of your trains yesterday, and I was wondering if anyone had handed it in.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: Right. Well, nothing's come in today that matches, I'm afraid. But if I take down some details and a description, we'll get in touch as soon as it turns up. Is that all right?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Yes, that'd be great. Thanks.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: OK, so first of all, can I have your name?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: It's Claire Dunleavy.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: Is that D, O, N, as in Donald?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: No, D, U, N. So it's D, U, N, L, E, A, V, Y.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: Got it. And your address?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Well, I've just moved, so it's not the Mount Lawley one any more. It's 22 Mill Point Road, South Perth.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: And what's the postcode there?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Er, I nearly said 6050, but that was my old one. The new one is 6151, that's 6, 1, 5, 1.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: Lovely. Now, you said you lost the bag yesterday. So that'd be Wednesday the 15th of June?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Oh, sorry, no, I've got my days mixed up. I actually lost it the evening before, on Tuesday, so it was the 14th. I didn't notice it was missing until the next morning.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: No problem. And roughly what time was the train?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Let me see. I finish work at 5.15, and I usually get the 5.30, but I missed it that day. So it was the 5.45.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: From the city out to Fremantle?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: That's right. I was meeting a friend for dinner down there.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: And do you remember which part of the train you sat in?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Um, normally I go for the middle carriage, because it stops right by the exit at Fremantle. But it was absolutely packed, so I walked all the way down to the back carriage and found a seat there.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: OK, that's really helpful. Now I'll need a description of the bag itself, and anything that was inside it.

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Sure. Well, it isn't a handbag or anything like that. It's a backpack, quite a small one.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: And what colour is it?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Most people think it's black, but it's actually dark green. It only looks black when the light's not very good.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: Is there a brand name on it, or anything else that would help us recognise it?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: The brand name's pretty much worn off, I'm afraid. And there used to be a keyring on the zip, but that fell off ages ago, so don't put that down. Oh, I know. There's a small Irish flag sewn onto the front pocket. My mum did that for me before I left home.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: That's perfect, that'll make it easy to spot. And what was in the backpack?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Well, luckily my purse and my phone were in my jacket. But my camera was in there, and a pair of sunglasses, and a paperback I was halfway through.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: Right. And just for our records, can you give me a rough idea of what it's all worth?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Hmm. The camera was about $400 when I bought it, but that was 3 years ago. And the bag itself was only about $40.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: So would you say around $440 altogether?

script.speaker: S2
script.text: No, I'd say less than that now, because the camera's quite old. Put down $320 for everything.

script.speaker: S1
script.text: OK, $320. If it's handed in, it'll be sent here to the main office at Perth Station, and you'll need to bring some photo ID to collect it.

script.speaker: S2
script.text: That's fine. How long do you keep things for?

script.speaker: S1
script.text: We hold everything for 3 months. Now, let me just take a mobile number, and I'll text you a reference number so you can check online as well.

script.speaker: S2
script.text: Great. Thank you so much.
